payload.name: Family-member expansion for who-in-family questions
payload.description: When a question asks who in a person's family experienced a condition or event, run supplementary searches for each family role combined with the condition before answering.
content: When a question asks who in a person's family has or experienced a condition/event (e.g., injured, sick, plays a sport), do not conclude from the named person's own memories alone.

First retrieve relationship memories to identify known family roles (son, partner, parents, etc.), then run additional searches combining each role with the condition/event terms (e.g., '<person> son <condition>').
If a family role has no matching memory after these searches, then it is safe to answer from the retrieved evidence; otherwise keep searching.

solves: A diagnosis of a family-level question (e.g., who was injured) showed that the agent retrieved only the named person's injury and missed a family member's injury stored in a separate memory. The rule to expand queries across family roles generalizes to any question asking who among a person's relatives has a condition, activity, or attribute, because such memories are often filed per individual rather than under the family unit.
